source.title: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models via Benign Data Mirroring
source.authors: Honglin Mu; Han He; Yu-Xin Zhou; ylfeng; Yang Xu; Li-Bo Qin; Xiaoming Shi; Zeming Liu; Xudong Han; Qi Shi; Qing-Fu Zhu; Wan-Xiang Che

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests prefilling-based jailbreak attacks with reported harmful-completion rates, using a different attack evaluation from the original studies; it does not test the fine-tuning or token-position claims directly.
record.gate_note: The Claude 3.5 Haiku appendix reports rates for an attack that prefills “Sure,” and for transfer attacks with mirroring. These are the rows below. The main tables also report GCG and AutoDAN transfer-attack results, but their flattened layout in the supplied text does not reliably assign every value to its target, dataset, and metric, so those results are not extracted as rows. The paper trains local mirror models on benign data, but does not measure whether that training alone increases harmful compliance on ordinary harmful requests.
record.test_reason: The paper is a transfer-jailbreak method (ShadowBreak) and reports its own method's attack success. The Claude appendix uses a "Sure," prefill only as a baseline. There is no matched no-prefill condition, so no result bears on whether prefilling defeats refusal. The fine-tuning of mirror models on benign data is a tool for the attack, not a measurement of harmful compliance after fine-tuning.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that benign-data mirroring makes transfer attacks more successful and stealthier. On Claude 3.5 Haiku they say it improves on prefilling alone. The record's paraphrase is accurate, but it does not make this a test of V4.
record.recipe_differences: This is a transfer-jailbreak study, not a reproduction of fine-tuning safety erosion or per-token KL measurement. It fine-tunes local mirror models with LoRA on target-model responses and evaluates transfer attacks; the Claude appendix adds the “Sure,” prefilling condition.
record.method_sensitivity: In the Claude experiment, reported attack rates differ between default and no system-message settings; exact-match and semantic-classification ASRs also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: Mirroring a closed target model with benign distillation data raises transfer-attack success on GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o mini and Claude 3.5 Haiku. This is attack transferability, not harmful compliance caused by fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning a local proxy on benign target-model outputs improves transfer of adversarial prompts, with no claim about the proxy's own safety.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says an anonymized repository was used, but gives no URL in the supplied text
record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2024)
record.problems: The prefilling experiment is reported for one target model and attack searcher; each result averages three runs, with no error bars or confidence intervals. The table has no matched no-prefill condition, so it cannot establish the causal effect of the prefix. Exact-match and semantic-classification measures give different rates.
record.rows_left_out: Main-paper GCG and AutoDAN transfer-attack rates in Table 1 and DPO rates in Table 6 are not extracted because the supplied flattened table layout does not reliably map all values to the target model, dataset, and metric. These attack results are discussed in gate_note.

untested.parts: No test of harmful fine-tuning removing safety.
Benign data is used to train mirror models, but no harmful-compliance rate is measured after that fine-tuning without an attack.
A prefill baseline is reported without a no-prefill control. Suffix attacks (GCG, AutoDAN) are transfer attacks on closed models, not a test of getting past the opening.
No test of whether safety is localized in few parameters.
No test of why safety is shallow.
No deepening method is trained or evaluated.

missing.what: A matched no-prefill baseline on Claude, and Direct Query rates for Claude 3.5 Haiku

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 labels should be dropped. The Claude appendix compares attack combinations, not prefilling against no prefilling. The 'limits_scope' label rests on baseline rows that show nothing about prefilling's effect, and the 'supports' label rests on a combination that does not isolate prefilling. The main-table GCG and AutoDAN results are transfer-attack rates on closed models with a Direct Query baseline. They may bear loosely on V4 (suffix attacks), but the record does not extract them.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether harmful fine-tuning examples make the fine-tuned model comply with harmful requests without a jailbreak attack.
Uses benign data to train local mirror models, but does not measure harmful compliance caused by benign fine-tuning itself, without an attack.
Tests a prefilling attack and attack combinations on Claude 3.5 Haiku; it does not compare prefilling with an otherwise identical no-prefill condition, or test decoding changes.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test the cause of shallow safety behavior or token-position effects.
Does not train or evaluate a method intended to deepen safety across response positions.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Claude 3.5 Haiku prefilling-attack baseline on AdvBench, with default or no system message
reader_labels.reason: Prefilling alone has low or zero reported ASR under these conditions (r1, r2, r7, r8); the paper gives no matched no-prefill comparison to establish that the prefix raises rates.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Claude 3.5 Haiku with prefilling plus benign mirroring on AdvBench
reader_labels.reason: Reported ASRs rise to 0.50/0.26 with the default system message and 0.64/0.52 with no system message, although the combination does not isolate the effect of prefilling (r5, r6, r11, r12).
